data.gender_notes: Manvendra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manvendra is a Sanskrit name derived from two words: Manas (mind) and Vendra (rule). The name signifies ruling the mind with the power of mantras and wisdom. This name is associated with powerful rulers and spiritual leaders in Hindu mythology. The name Manvendra carries the meaning “Rule by Mantra” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manvendra usually hope their child will grow to embody rule by mantra and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Manvendra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rule by Mantra.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manvendra total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.spiritual_significance: Manvendra is a deeply spiritual name, implying control over one's mind and thoughts. In Hinduism, controlling the mind is a crucial aspect of spiritual growth and enlightenment. historical_references.reference: Manvendra was the son of King Manu, the lawgiver of mankind in Hindu mythology. He is considered as the founder of the Lunar Dynasty of Kings.
historical_references.context: Manvendra is a significant figure in Hindu mythology and is often considered as the first king of the Lunar Dynasty, which was one of the two major dynasties in ancient India.

historical_references.reference: Manvendra was also known as Manvendra Maharaj or Manvendra Pal. He is considered as a perfect ruler and is believed to have ruled with great wisdom and justice during his reign.
historical_references.context: Manvendra is also known from historical records as the last independent king of Gujarat's Chalukya dynasty. He is remembered for his just rule and his contributions to the development of Gujarat.
